Subject: Re: sudden latency/error spike impacting Brightline prod (tier: gold)

Quick triage notes — findings first, then suggested next actions.

Findings (observed on affected hosts 10.4.21.[12-14]):
- KV snapshot shows top 3 keys consumed ~72% of prefix-cache evictions during the window. These keys had very long-lived requests (mean request duration ~2.3s) that kept the batch head occupied.
- Our batching lanes are ordered FIFO per-worker; when a worker's head-of-line request holds the KV lock while waiting on remote data, subsequent short requests are queued behind it (classic HOL blockage).
- Prefetch enabled for this tenant aggressively warms prefixes which increases lock hold time when the warmer collides with an already-slow request.
- Eviction churn (TTL-based) increased because the hot keys' read-modify cycles prevent timely background compaction; CPU and KV GC spikes correlate with p99 increases.

Immediate mitigations I can apply now (low-risk first):
1) Temporarily disable tenant-level prefix prefetch to reduce lock-hold amplification (5-10 min change).
2) Reduce batching window from 12ms -> 4ms on impacted pool to limit queue depth (this trades some throughput for tail latency).
3) Enable per-key request queueing cap: if a key's waiting queue > N, route new requests to degraded model variant to avoid long tail.
4) Kick a controlled worker restart for the three affected hosts after steps 1-3 to allow prefix caches to rebalance.

If we need faster restoration and have agreement from the customer: evict the top-10 hot keys and clear their prefix entries — this will cause a short cache warm but should remove the interlock.

I'll start 1-3 now; please confirm we have permission to do 4 and the eviction if required.

Karthik

Subject: Post-mitigation summary: Brightline — head-of-line interlock resolved, next steps

Amit / Sophie —

Follow-up summary of actions and current status:
- 09:30: disabled tenant prefix prefetch.
- 09:35: reduced batching window (12ms -> 4ms) on the impacted GPU pool.
- 09:42: initiated controlled restarts on hosts 10.4.21.12–14 after ensuring request re-routing.
- 09:58: evicted top-10 hot keys from prefix store when we still observed >1.2s p99 following prior steps.

Outcome: by ~10:15 PST p99 fell from 2.1s -> 310ms and error rate dropped below 0.3%. Token throughput recovered to ~87% of baseline. No customer-visible data loss.

Attachments included: kv_profile_20261112.csv (before/after snapshots), heapdump_excerpt.txt (truncated), mitigation-checklist.pdf.

Recommended follow-ups (customers + internal):
- Engineering: implement a tenant-level per-key queue cap and an automated fallback to degraded-variant when a hot-key interlock is detected (INF-4421).
- Product: add a per-tenant prefetch throttle and expose an opt-out flag for customers that perform large key-level IO patterns.
- Ops/CS: run a joint post-mortem with Brightline in 72 hours; prepare a goodwill credit proposal tied to remediation time (Marissa).

We will produce a full incident report with timelines and metric graphs within 48 hours.

Thanks for the patience — will keep tracking.

Karthik
